texts.preamble: Smt Madhu A S vs Sri Gopala Krishna K M @Vimal on 23 December, 2024 1 Crl.Misc.190/2024 Judgment
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed a petition under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, against the respondents, seeking various forms of relief as provided under the Act. The Petitioner is the legally wedded wife of Respondent No. 1, and their marriage was solemnized on 18.11.2009 at Kabadi Shankarsa Gangubai Kalyana Mantapa, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru, according to Hindu rites and customs, in the presence of their families, friends, and well-wishers. The couple has a daughter from their marriage. However, shortly after the marriage, Respondent No. 1 began harassing the Petitioner. Respondent No. 2 stated that Respondent No. 1 was irresponsible and that his behavior towards the Petitioner was Crl.Misc.No.190/2024 JUDGMENT reckless. Within a month of marriage, the Petitioner became pregnant, but her announcement was met with indifference from Respondent No. 1 and his family. The Petitioner experienced severe morning sickness during pregnancy and endured further verbal abuse from Respondent Nos. 1 and 2. 1 When the Petitioner suffered from kidney stones, Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 pressured her into having an abortion, which she initially resisted. Despite seeking a second opinion, the doctor was aligned with Respondent No. 1 and also advised abortion. The Petitioner was isolated and treated as an outcast in her matrimonial home, enduring mental and physical abuse. b. The Petitioner continued to face abuse from Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 for not agreeing to abort, and Respondent No. 1 threatened to throw her out of the house. Ultimately, she was coerced into having an abortion. Additionally, Respondent No. 1's alcoholism and erratic behavior added to the Petitioner's suffering. He prevented her from visiting her family, and at times, confiscated her gold jewelry to sell for personal use. The Petitioner became pregnant Crl.Misc.No.190/2024 JUDGMENT again, but Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 continued to demand an abortion. After enduring more harassment, the Petitioner eventually moved to her parental home, but continued to be subjected to abuse, including being forced to work while receiving no support from Respondent No. 1. c. During his employment at a bar, Respondent No. 1 would come home drunk, adding to the Petitioner's distress. He later secured a job at a company in Lalbagh Road, where the Petitioner discovered he was in a relationship with another woman. When she confronted him, he became abusive and violent, leaving the house for several days. Over time, Respondent No. 1 continued to emotionally and financially manipulate the Petitioner, including transferring large sums of money into her account, leading to legal complications. When the Petitioner questioned these transactions, she was threatened, physically assaulted, and ultimately thrown out of the house with her daughter. The Respondent's actions escalated, culminating in a complaint against him for fraud. He also subjected the Petitioner to harassment via social media, where he posted defamatory content about her and her family. The Petitioner was repeatedly contacted by strangers due to her personal information being posted on dating apps, causing severe mental distress. Throughout their 14 years of marriage, Respondent No. 1's cruel behavior caused the Petitioner constant mental and physical harm, including repeated instances of violence, financial abuse, and emotional manipulation. The Petitioner was forced to leave the marital home for her safety, and she now lives with her parents. The Petitioner has suffered immense mental and physical distress due to Respondent No. 1's actions, which have led to a breakdown in the marriage. She prays for relief from the cruel treatment she has endured, and for the Hon'ble Court to consider further evidence during the trial. The cause of action for this petition arose on 18.11.2009, with the marriage and subsequent harassment by Respondent No. 1. As the Petitioner resides in Bengaluru, this Hon'ble Crl.Misc.No.190/2024 JUDGMENT Court has jurisdiction to hear this matter. Hence, the Petitioner prays that the petition be allowed. 3. After the registration of the petition, notices were duly issued to the respondents, and these notices were successfully served upon them. Despite being served, the respondents failed to appear before the Court on the scheduled date. As a result, the respondents were placed ex-parte, and the matter was subsequently set down for trial. 4. To substantiate her case, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.5 and closed her side. She contended that, her marriage was solemnized on 18.11.2009 at Kabadi Shankarsa Gangubai Kalyana Mantapa, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru, as per Hindu Rites and Customs, in the presence of parent's, friends and well wishers. Out of their wedlock, they have begotten one girl child. During the stay of petitioner in the house of respondents, the respondent No.1 has given ill-treatment to the petitioner and drove out the petitioner without providing any maintenance. The petitioner averred in the petition about the ill- treatment and domestic violence committed by the respondent and also deposed as Pw.1 by reiterating the petition averments and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.5. Ex.P.1 is the Marriage Invitation Card, Ex.P.2 is the Marriage Photos, Ex.P.3 is theCertified copy of FIR, Ex.P.4 is the WhatApp messages and Ex.P.5 is the Facebook details. Upon perusal of these documents, relationship between the petitioner, her child and respondents is not in dispute. 10. Despite the service of notice, the respondents have failed to appear before the Court. . Furthermore, the respondent No.1 has deserted and neglected both the petitioner and her child, Crl.Misc.No.190/2024 JUDGMENT failing to provide any maintenance or support.
texts.arguments: Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner has successfully proven that Smt Madhu A S vs Sri Gopala Krishna K M @Vimal on 23 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18326449/ 3 she has been subjected to domestic violence by the respondents The petitioner has provided testimony that Respondent No.1 has not only failed to provide any maintenance but has also neglected his responsibility to make adequate provisions for her residence. The petitioner has further averred that Respondent No.1 is employed at a company called Papier and is earning more than Rs.90,000/- per month. However, despite these claims, the petitioner has not provided any documentary evidence or formal proof to substantiate the alleged income of Respondent No.1. 12. While the petitioner's assertion regarding Respondent No.1's earnings remains unproven, it can be reasonably inferred, based on the fact that Respondent No.1 is Crl.Misc.No.190/2024 JUDGMENT employed, that he is likely earning a substantial income and is therefore capable of fulfilling his financial obligations towards the petitioner. In response, the petitioner has stated that she is employed as an Admin at Global Mobility and receives a salary of Rs.20,000/- per month.

texts.respondent_arguments: The petitioner has further averred that Respondent No.1 is employed at a company called Papier and is earning more than Rs.90,000/- per month. However, despite these claims, the petitioner has not provided any documentary evidence or formal proof to substantiate the alleged income of Respondent No.1. 12. While the petitioner's assertion regarding Respondent No.1's earnings remains unproven, it can be reasonably inferred, based on the fact that Respondent No.1 is Crl.Misc.No.190/2024 JUDGMENT employed, that he is likely earning a substantial income and is therefore capable of fulfilling his financial obligations towards the petitioner. In response, the petitioner has stated that she is employed as an Admin at Global Mobility and receives a salary of Rs.20,000/- per month.
